name: Peru
sources: GDP $26.4bn and 22.0m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $26.410bn and 22,014,771). The dollar figure is the least reliable in this file: with the inti collapsing and a split exchange market, any dollar conversion of Peruvian output in 1990 is an artefact of which rate is used, and estimates run from roughly $22bn to $30bn. Real GDP fell 5.1% in 1990 on top of 12.3% in 1989, a cumulative contraction of about a quarter over three years, hence a TFP trend of -1.5%/yr.

INFLATION IS NOT THE TRANSCRIBED PRINT. INEI records 7,650% for 1990 as an annual average, the worst in Peruvian history and the second worst in the hemisphere after Nicaragua. On the fraction-of-1 convention that is 76.5, twenty-five times the 3.0 ceiling economy.rs clamps to on the first tick. The file ships 2.950 and records the truth here, exactly as brazil.json, poland.json and yugoslavia.json do.

interest_rate 2.9 is a stand-in on the same grounds: nominal rates tracked inflation into the thousands of percent, and the schema's coupling rule forbids entering them beside a clamped inflation figure. The Fujishock of 8 August 1990 that ended this is not scripted; the sim's central bank has to find the stabilisation itself.
Tax take 9% of GDP: central government tax revenue had fallen to about 8.1% of GDP by 1989-90, near the point at which a state stops functioning, which is the substantive fact this row carries.

Debt 0.80: external debt about $20bn at end-1990 (World Bank), roughly 76% of GDP and in arrears since Alan Garcia capped debt service at 10% of export earnings in July 1985 and the IMF declared Peru ineligible in 1986.
Oil 0.13 mbd: about 130,000 bbl/d from the northern jungle and Talara, down by a third from the early 1980s.

Stability 22, the lowest figure in this roster, and it is transcribed: Sendero Luminoso and the MRTA held emergency-zone provinces containing over half the population, the war had killed some 20,000 people by 1990, and cholera arrived in January 1991. Separatism 0.06 — Sendero sought to replace the state, not to leave it. Defence 2.3% of GDP, strength 6, an army fighting an internal war it was not built for.
